text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- MONETARY BASE CONTRACTS
Brazil's monetary base unexpectedly contracted by 574 million reais ($549.3 million) in January due to the new so-called CPMF cheque tax and $1 billion capital outflows.
-- COMPANIES COULD FINANCE EXPORT FUND
Businesses are studying the idea of financing a fund to promote exports by raising money via a contribution of 0.3 percent on total imports to be paid by companies.
-- LLOYDS BANK BUYS MULTIPLIC ASSETS
Lloyds Bank is to pay $600 million to its MEC Empreendimentos partner in Banco Multiplic for all of Multiplic's assets and the bank's financial arm.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- INSOLVENCY HIGHEST IN NINE MONTHS
Consumer insolvency in Sao Paulo has risen 44.2 percent in January compared with the same month last year, the largest increase in nine months.
-- PSDB BACKS ANTONIO CARLOS MAGALHAES IN SENATE
Antonio Carlos Magalhaes is favorite to win the vote for the Senate presidency after formal backing from the PSDB party.
O GLOBO
-- CARDOSO SANCTIONS AUTOMATIC ORGAN DONATION
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will sanction a bill that would make all Brazilians automatic organ donors unless they specifically register not to be donors.
-- CAIXA ECONOMICA FEDERAL GIVES MORE MONEY TO MIDDLE CLASS
Caixa Economica Federal is due to make more funds available to middle class homebuyers worth some 200 million to 300 million reais.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151 ($ = 1.045 Brazilian Reais)
